---
title: "Income inequality"
description: "How evenly income is shared, before and after tax and social welfare, compared with the EU."
---

The Gini coefficient is a common measure of how evenly income is shared. It would be 0 if every household had the same income and 100 if one household had all of it.

Income from work and investments is shared unevenly in Ireland, but tax and social welfare narrow the gap a lot. In 2025, the Gini coefficient for household income before tax and social welfare was 45.5. After them, it was 27.4.

{{< chart poverty-inequality >}}

## Compared with the EU

After tax and social welfare, income in Ireland is shared a little more evenly than in the EU as a whole. In 2025, Ireland's Gini coefficient was 27.2, compared with 29.2 for the EU, the 8th lowest of the 27 countries.
